text:
jia: quick check-in on routing policy change I'm experimenting with: instead of a single score we return a small vector: {latency_est_ms, cost_est_units, region_affinity_score}. admission then applies tenant budget + slo caps to pick. idea is to keep adapters simple and push policy wiring to admission. feedback?

ben: sounds sensible. two thoughts: 1) units need normalization (a cost unit on A100 != cost unit on L4). we should define a canonical cost unit per device class or include device_class tag. 2) region_affinity_score needs to be composable with tenant region preference (e.g., tenant prefers eu with penalty for non-eu).

katie: about normalization agree. propose adapters emit est_cost with an explicit unit like "cost_nanos" and we keep a conversion table (device->multiplier) in admission. avoids adapters knowing pricing.

omar: caution: adding more fields increases data sent at decision time which is fine, but we need to make sure scorer latency doesn't regress. can we make est_* optional and fall back to legacy scalar score? adapters should be backward compatible.

jia: yes fallback planned. adapters that don't emit vectors get mapped via legacy mapping in admission. also we'll add a small shim in sidecar to augment missing fields with defaults from device profiles.

lucas: rollout concerns: if admission changes interpretation (e.g., converts cost units differently) we might see abrupt routing shifts. need a deterministic simulation path: replay historical requests, feed into new admission logic, and produce per-tenant delta reports.

katie: can we run that simulation in shadow mode in prod for a few hours? sample 0.1% traffic, compute proposed route but don't execute. collect metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, cost, reserved_pool_hit_rate.

ben: also add a fairness signal: pct_reserved_served_by_tier. low-tier tenants shouldn't be starved from reserved capacity by aggressive cost routing. define guardrails: reserved_quota_floor per tenant.

omar: about SLO compliance: admission must enforce tenant-level hard caps. if proposed route violates SLO, admission should rewrite to a route that meets SLO (even if cost higher). we need explicit parameter: "slo_priority": high|normal|best_effort.

jia: implementation sketch: 1) adapter: return optional est fields + device_class tag 2) admission: convert est_cost via device multipliers, compute utility = w_latency*latency_norm + w_cost*cost_norm + w_region*region_score; apply tenant budget multiplier and SLO override 3) admission emits chosen route and a decision rationale header for tracing.

lucas: decision rationale is great for debugging. please include top-3 alternative routes and their utilities in rationale (capped length).

katie: testing: unit tests for conversion table, property tests for monotonicity (if latency_est decreases, utility should not increase for latency-heavy weightings), and integration replay tests.

infra-bot: ci: routing-admission-tests passed on branch jia/routing-vector (build 4821) :white_check_mark:

ben: telemetry requirements: per-device inflight, per-route queue_time_ms histogram, completions by budget tag, reserved_pool_failures (when a reserved device rejects due to quota). these are needed for tuning the multipliers.

omar: add a circuit-breaker: if queue_time_ms p99 on any device_class > threshold for >1m, admission should disable low-budget routing to that class for 5m. helps prevent cascading tails.

jia: nice. I'll draft the minimal RFC: adapter changes (optional est fields + device tag), admission conversion table + weights, rationale header spec, simulation checklist (replay + shadow), and circuit-breaker thresholds. will assign PRs for sidecar shim and admission changes.

katie: please include a short compatibility plan for library adapters in clients (how they fall back).

jia: will do. thanks all.
